title: Seed-Sensitivity of Safety Features Across SAE Reruns

original_idea.body:
# Seed-Sensitivity of Safety Features Across SAE Reruns

**Problem:** SAEs trained with different seeds converge to different feature sets; a safety feature found in one but not a sibling means single-SAE safety claims are fragile.

**Direction:** Take 2+ openly released SAEs for the same model/layer, match safety-relevant features via activation-correlation, report stable vs seed-specific fraction.

**Why it matters:** Establishes whether SAE-based safety findings replicate. No training, public weights.

**Relevant context:** Neuronpedia/SAELens; Open Phil RFP.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (reproducibility is a prerequisite for SAE-based monitoring) but a step from any deployed safety guarantee.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Activation-correlation matching across pre-trained SAEs; no training, guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (stable-feature fraction) with few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public weights, reproducibility audit labs won't prioritize; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on public SAEs/models; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: SAE seed-instability is known; quantifying it for safety features specifically may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: SAE instability is documented broadly; the safety-feature-specific replication may be open.
